newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents lower Friday as traders expect the market to give back some of Thursday's gains after the resolution of a strike by portworkers in Brazil.
Portworkers returned to work at Brazil's key coffee loading port of Santos Friday after a 24-hour work stoppage in protest of delays in receiving their full April salary.

Thursday, New York arabica futures ended mostly higher, bolstered by news of the Brazilian portworkers' work stoppage. July closed up 5.50 cents at 216.90 cents a lb after trading from 219.50 to 209.50. Spot May fell 5.65 to 240.00, while the back months gained 0.50 to 3.15.
May/July spread shrunk to 23.10 cents today from 34.25 at the close on Tuesday, while July/September widened to 22.40 cents from 20.05 cents.
Technically, traders pegged near-term July support at 214.49, followed by a strong layer at 209.00. July resistance was seen at 220.00, followed by 225.00, its life-of-contract high.
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks increased by 750 bags, to 25,419 bags as of May 7. There were 17,743 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were mostly lower at midday Friday, retracing from eight-week highs hit early in the session. LIFFE July was down $20 at the break, to $1,760, after peaking at $1,793.
